Seemingly mild disagreements could get surprisingly intense today. If you’re not careful, you might find yourself picking fights you don’t actually want — with people you don’t actually have a problem with. So before things get heated, take a step back and ask yourself whether you really need to start an argument right now. If there’s nothing meaningful at stake, consider letting it go. Find somewhere more worthwhile to direct your confrontational energy.

In general, you don’t mind being alone. You pride yourself on being independent. But today, you could feel surprisingly needy. You’ll want to be near the people you care about and to feel seen by them. But don’t expect your friends to magically intuit that you want to spend time together. You’ll have to make a point of seeking out their company. They might assume you’re happy doing things on your own; if that’s not the case right now, then say so.

When people are rude or careless, you try to be understanding. Maybe they’re stressed about personal problems you’re unaware of, or maybe you said something tactless without realizing it. But while your compassion is laudable, you don’t have to be endlessly accommodating. That’s especially true when people take advantage of your generosity. Today, continue being kind — but you’re allowed to hope for some kindness in return. If others refuse to give it, it might be time to reconsider your relationships.
Buy Claire Comstock-Gay’s book, Madame Clairevoyant’s Guide to the Stars, here.

items.title: Here’s Your November Horoscope
items.description: November opens in the deep end. The new moon rises in uncompromising Scorpio on Nov. 9. Prepare to get real about what you want. What are you finally ready to release in order to get it? This isn’t the time for half-measures or surface-level intentions. The ch
items.author: Alexandria Lettman
paragraphs: November opens in the deep end. The new moon rises in uncompromising Scorpio on Nov. 9. Prepare to get real about what you want. What are you finally ready to release in order to get it? This isn’t the time for half-measures or surface-level intentions. The choices you make now carry a lasting weight, so consider them carefully.
The fog finally lifts on Nov. 13, when Mercury retrograde ends in Scorpio. It may feel easier to pick up the thread of a conversation, decision, or idea you have been circling since late October.

The next day, Venus follows suit when it stations direct in Libra. The culmination of this retrograde is the exhale you’ve been waiting for. Notice what has changed about what you are willing to give and receive to sustain a relationship.

After all of Scorpio season’s intensity, the sun’s ingress into Sagittarius on Nov. 22 swings open a window and lets the light back in. Adventure and hope are back on the table. Look forward and aim high.

Electric energy buzzes around the full moon in Gemini on Nov. 24. Uranus, the planet of innovation and change, links up with the bright supermoon. A breakthrough could be on the horizon, the kind that leads you to finally share what’s on your mind. However, one thing remains uncertain: how other people will respond. Don’t let this stop you from speaking your truth.

When motivated Mars enters precise Virgo on Nov. 25, effort, discipline, and methodical action beat impulsivity. The goals that have been gaining momentum now require focus and a plan of execution. Roll up your sleeves and dive into the real, productive work — then relax the next day with some turkey and cranberry sauce.
Happy birthday, Sagittarius!

Good news, Aries! The words you couldn’t find in October may spring to mind with clarity this month. That conversation you’ve been dreading could turn out to be the one that actually frees you. Don’t be afraid to revisit a situation that has tested your honesty, trust, and ability to be vulnerable.

Whether you are hashing out a shared financial burden or getting intimate with a partner, you could walk into Sagittarius season (beginning on Nov. 22) feeling optimistic about what lies ahead. Rather than letting your thoughts fester, speak up in the moment. Luck is on your side.

All relationships have ups and downs, but they shouldn’t feel permanently exhausting. After the intimate Scorpio new moon on Nov. 9, you may have a clearer idea of what’s worth fighting for. How can you turn over a new leaf?

By mid-month, complicated issues at work can be resolved through stronger collaboration. Remember your worth and think twice before you pick up other people’s responsibilities again. In late November, a breakthrough might inspire you to reallocate your time, energy, money, and resources. This is your green light to invest in your creative side hustle or a promising romantic connection.

For you, the whole month is building toward the full moon in your sign on Nov. 24. But first, you should lay the groundwork. In early November, you need to adjust your priorities. Cut out whatever’s been draining your energy, and focus on habits and activities that fill your cup.
An old passion project or romantic connection could find its worth again ahead of Sagittarius season (beginning on Nov. 22). If you feel hopeful, dive in.

Finally, the full moon brings surprising clarity on what needs to change within in order for you to manifest the life you really want. Don’t underestimate what can click into place when you let go. Only worry about what you can control.

Don’t be surprised when the passion, connection, and spark you thought was lost makes a dramatic return. The Scorpio new moon on Nov. 9 creates space for you to get clear on your values, hidden desires, and what will truly make you happy. This kind of self-reflection could be a powerful magnet for love.

However, don’t expect to figure out all the answers at once. Clarity will come gradually and certain outcomes will remain uncertain. On Nov. 24, try not to worry about the missing pieces when the full moon lights up your psychological sector. Choose your next step and see it through.

Unresolved feelings have been churning in the background, creating a moody start to the month. However, when you are committed to building bridges — not burning them — you may finally make progress. Lead with honesty and speak with care.

The second half of the month revives the fire in your social life, but concerns about your budget and schedule could hinder your ability to live in the moment. Don’t be irresponsible, but stay as flexible as possible. Your friendships are worth their weight in gold.

Confusion turns into clarity this month. Mark your calendar for Nov. 13, when Mercury retrograde switches gears, alleviating the pressure you feel to dissect the subliminal meaning of every text or email. In order to get conversations moving again, you don’t necessarily need to find the perfect words for expressing yourself. Start by recognizing that your voice has value, even if others disagree with your perspective.

Around mid-month, your focus shifts toward pursuing your life’s purpose. On Nov. 25, calculating Mars enters your sign, boosting your energy, discipline, and drive. Forge your own way rather than adhering to other people’s standards. Your journey is yours alone.

Venus, your ruling planet, is in retrograde from Oct. 3 - Nov. 14. Your attention has been focused on the hard work of examining who you are, what you want, and whether you’re willing to ask for it. However, don’t expect immediate progress once this phase wraps up. Acknowledge where self-doubt still keeps you stuck.

A deep hunger for meaningful conversation kicks in during the second half of the month. Whether you engage in thoughtful debates, pick up a new book, or listen to a podcast that blows your mind, prepare for your outlook to radically change — or at least you’ll plant new seeds.

November opens with a deep personal reset. The new moon rises in your sign on Nov. 9, setting the stage for new goals, intentions, and ideas around how you want to show up in the world. You can reinvent yourself at any moment, even on a random Wednesday, if you’re tired of holding back.

Your self-awareness sharpens on Nov. 13. Mercury travels forward in your sign, dissolving the intense air of mystery you’ve been projecting that’s kept some people at arm’s length. If you are emerging from an extended period of solitude, be wary of rushing into trust, consistency, and comfort. Nothing worth having is built overnight. People will treat you more warmly if you act with confidence and generosity.
Sagittarius (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
You’ve been bravely confronting your fears for months, and you’ve finally earned a break. Relax and release the negativity!

The real shift comes on Nov. 22, when the sun reinvigorates your sign. Suddenly, you’re back to your best self. You don’t need to force optimism, and adventures seem to be looking for you, not the other way around. Pursue what makes you feel alive. That said, your partner may ask where they fit into your solo exploration.
If relationships don’t steal your focus at the end of the month, your career might take to the spotlight. Move with a plan.
Capricorn (Dec. 21-Jan. 18)

Any uncertainty surrounding your career or public image will resolve in the first two weeks of the month. A relationship with a boss or mentor may move in a positive new direction, or you might find yourself getting involved with a community that shares your values. Either way, welcome the support!

As a hard-working Capricorn, you struggle to accept that rest can be productive. Everyone needs to recharge, and when Sagittarius season begins on Nov. 22, it’s your turn. Use introspection as a healing practice. As a result of your quiet time, you may be inspired to make a change in your lifestyle. Once your energy returns, set things into motion as soon as possible.
Aquarius (Jan. 19-Feb. 17)

It’s difficult to plan your life when you are questioning the very principles that have long underpinned your definition of success. Give yourself grace for the slow progress made this autumn. You may be stumbling toward something more valuable than you realize: a renewed sense of passion and purpose. Once Mercury and Venus station direct on Nov. 13 and 14, follow your heart with unwavering loyalty. Share your inspiration and the ideas that have motivated you with your friends or followers.

If you’re single or casually dating, a sudden peak in your love life could coincide with the flirtatious Gemini full moon on Nov. 24. Just keep in mind that you are in an important season of building. Enjoy what feels light and playful, but be cautious of entering a serious commitment until you are more certain of what you are able to invest.

If a new course of study or philosophical idea calls your name, go all in. You may discover a belief or intellectual field that resonates with where you are now rather than who you used to be. Before you hand over your credit card, however, wait for the hazy retrograde energy to settle around Nov. 14.

If you are itching for a bigger life during the second half of the month, the right move is to follow your feelings rather than your fears. Be discerning about who you team up with this month. Make sure they share your enthusiasm and seriousness about building in a new direction.
For more, check out your tarot reading.

items.title: 5 Spicy Friends-To-Lovers Books ‘Nobody Wants This’ Fans Will Swoon Over
items.description: The central love story of Nobody Wants This may be the star-crossed pairing between “hot rabbi” Noah and sex podcaster Joanne, but in Season 3, a new fling enters the chat. And friends-to-lovers fans... this one’s for you.
items.author: Grace Wehniainen
paragraphs: The central love story of Nobody Wants This may be the star-crossed pairing between “hot rabbi” Noah and sex podcaster Joanne, but in Season 3, a new fling enters the chat. And friends-to-lovers fans... this one’s for you.

Brought into each other’s orbit by their respective siblings’ relationship, Morgan and Sasha have spent several seasons developing their own special friendship — one defined by playful banter that even they’re rarely sure is friendly or flirty. (As Morgan told Sasha in Season 1, “Stop saying that it’s not weird when we both know that it kind of is.”)

In the latest entry, they finally hook up, and while fans might debate the specifics of their fling, there’s no denying that the friends-to-lovers trope brings a special kind of buzz. That built-in intimacy can lend itself to sweet, humorous repartee — there’s no need to play brooding or aloof when you know someone that well.
Need some more? Here are seven spicy friends-to-lovers books that echo the playful passion and relationship conundrums of Nobody Wants This.
The Roommate Risk by Talia Hibbert

After sharing a passionate night in college, Jasmine and Rahul decide to be just friends. Best friends. But seven years later, a plumbing emergency forces them into close proximity — leaving them to reckon with feelings that never really went away.
Funny Feelings by Tarah DeWitt

Stand-up comedian Farley is best friends with her manager, Meyer. When a career opportunity prompts them to begin a fake relationship, their closeness takes on a new (and deliciously passionate) form.
When Javi Dumped Mari by Mia Sosa

Though he’s had feelings for her since college, Javi’s insecurities lead him to believe his best friend Mari is unattainable. By the time he feels worthy of her, Mari’s engaged — and he’ll have to make his feelings known before she says “I do” in a countdown to the altar sweetly reminiscent of My Best Friend’s Wedding.
Hook, Line, and Sinker by Tessa Bailey

Much like Morgan in Nobody Wants This, Hannah meets Fox through her sister’s relationship, and the two become good friends. But when actor Hannah moves to Fox’s coastal town to shoot a movie, they discover a romantic tension that’s too reel to ignore.
Romancing Mister Bridgerton by Julia Quinn

There’s a Bridgerton book for every trope, and friends-to-lovers is executed beautifully in Romancing Mister Bridgerton. Penelope has long nursed a crush on her family friend, Colin, and while their union brings some obstacles to work out (including Pen’s secret gig as the ton’s juiciest gossip), all those years of pining have some seriously steamy payoff.

items.title: Exclusive: 'RHOSLC' Star Bronwyn Newport Dishes On The Upcoming 'Traitors' Season
items.description: Bronwyn Newport knows how to make an entrance. The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City star has made a name for herself by wearing outfits that test the limits of what might be considered appropriate, normal, or even wearable. (Rainbow feathered Dolce & Gabbana
items.author: Rachel Lapidos
paragraphs: Bronwyn Newport knows how to make an entrance. The Real Housewives of Salt Lake City star has made a name for herself by wearing outfits that test the limits of what might be considered appropriate, normal, or even wearable. (Rainbow feathered Dolce & Gabbana coat, anyone?) Her beauty philosophy, however, is a different story. “Beauty-wise, it’s always very, very tried-and-true for me,” she tells Bustle.

Rather than chasing an entirely new look, Newport, 41, focuses on skin health and preserving what makes her feel like herself. “For me, such a big part of beauty is who you naturally are,” she says. “I’ve obviously had a rhinoplasty. But I always want a big, beautiful smile — that’s always the finishing look, where you are yourself.”

It’s why her partnership with Colgate Optic White is such a natural fit. It's part of her everyday getting-ready routine, and she recently appeared at the brand’s activation at Bravo Fan Fest in Charleston, South Carolina. “I always have this big goofy grin everywhere I go,” she says. “I never look like I’ve been there before or I’m used to it or I’m cool. I always look like [I’m] giddy to be invited to the opening of an envelope.” For Newport, it’s about making sure “the health behind my skin and my teeth and my hair is done properly.”

Still, being a Housewife has made her more aware of how her appearance is perceived. Her imperfect teeth became a talking point among viewers early on, for example — but she’s learned to separate other people’s opinions from her own. “It’s hard to put yourself out there in every way on the show, especially your physical self, to be consumed and digested and discussed,” she says. “But I also really live for a woman in the year of our Lord 2026 being like, ‘No, this is what I want to look like, and this is how I want to feel.’”
Ahead, Newport opens up about filming The Traitors, the fan reactions she’s still processing, and why she’s approaching her next chapter with an open mind.
What is your favorite beauty treatment, and what’s the last one you treated yourself to?

It’s always about really great skin prep. I’m a big believer in retinol and lasers. I get a lot of glam done and my hair done, and when I don’t, I really don’t. I’m a ChapStick-and-mascara person. I said this in my first confessional ever that “sexy” is not really my aesthetic.
Your fashion is super adventurous and maximalist. Do you take the same approach to beauty, or do you keep certain parts more classic?

My approach has always been that the clothes are the star of the show. I’m not even the star of the show — it’s the outfits I put together. Beauty-wise, I stick with products that I know and have loved and used forever. It’s about the simplicity of knowing that all of that is taken care of and elevated and fabulous.
There were a lot of comments online about how you reacted in the episode where you took your castmates to San Francisco. How are you handling them?

It’s a lot. It’s so nice when something I do or say resonates with people. I was sharing quite a bit about what it feels like to be in a new chapter. San Francisco was home for me for so long, and so many people were appreciative of what I shared about publicly going through a separation and pending divorce.

One of the beautiful things about sharing my life on the show is getting to physically watch yourself and ask, “Wow, was that a choice that I liked? Was this a way that I responded?” I’ve realized I tend to act a certain way, and I don’t know if I love that.

There was some feedback this week about the way I handled certain things that made me think, “Yeah, that’s fair. I could have handled that better.” I don’t know that I’ll ever get another opportunity to respond to a diss at a party celebrating my separation, but if I do, I’m now armed with all the right ways to do it.
Has the “Hypocrisy & Bulls*it” song grown on you at all?
No. Shockingly enough, it has not. I have a feeling I will never hear the end of it, but it’ll just be one of those earworms that I have to deal with.
What can you say about the Traitors experience, and who were you most surprised to see in the castle?

I was surprised to see everyone because they do such a good job of keeping it quiet. I know that everyone was surprised to see me because I didn’t tell a soul. I was trying to buy things undercover, shopping at all kinds of different places and buying vintage so nobody would think, “Why is Bronwyn buying all this plaid?”

It was so fun. That’s maybe one of the last special things in the world: truly getting to surprise somebody. It’s a beautiful production to work on, and they’ve put together a cool group of people and a fabulous game.

I don’t always smile so much on Housewives. The dinner-party games usually aren’t smile-inducing. But on Traitors, I was grinning the whole time, running through the Scottish Highlands, being like, “I’m at work right now!” as we’re doing a challenge, or I’m wearing some crazy vintage outfit and arguing with somebody about whether I’m a Traitor.
Would you say that being a Housewife has made you better at reading people, or does it make you more suspicious of people?
A little bit of both. I like to think that I can see a train wreck coming now that I’ve been through so many Housewife dinners. I tend to feel the storm building as the entrées are ordered.

But it also makes me a little suspicious. I wanted to be so good at the game aspect of Traitors, but there’s no real way to plan for it. You never know what your role will be, how it will evolve, or who else will be there. The best strategy is to have no strategy. You’ll get to see how that plays out for me — pun intended — as I make a new strategy every day.
What is something you’re excited to explore or embrace in this next chapter of your life that you might not have been ready for a year ago?

Oh my gosh, everything. This was a lot more change and upheaval than I thought it would be. I always like to say that I’m dumb, not stupid, but sometimes I’m like, “Wow, this was very different from what I thought it was going to be.” I thought I really understood what a separation and divorce was going to look like, and I did not.

It’s interesting to sit with the idea that there’s a lot of grief and sadness and closure, which always tend to have a negative connotation, but that it can also bring so much optimism and hope. The dual-edged nature of that is that everything is possible again, and that’s a really beautiful thing to be able to say. I don’t know if I’ll enjoy or stick with everything I try in this new era of my life, but it’s fun to try things out.
This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

items.title: Glow Recipe's Blur Balm, Tate McRae's First Perfume, & 21 More October Beauty Drops
items.description: October might just be the perfect month. It’s not too hot, not too cold (all you need is a light jacket), the foliage is pretty enough to make an eyeshadow palette jealous, and you can finally wear your emotional support blazer again. And making this already p
items.author: Rachel Lapidos
paragraphs: October might just be the perfect month. It’s not too hot, not too cold (all you need is a light jacket), the foliage is pretty enough to make an eyeshadow palette jealous, and you can finally wear your emotional support blazer again. And making this already picturesque month even better? The best beauty launches hitting shelves are just as good as the scenery.

Haus Labs, for one, introduced a liquid bronzer that delivers a summer glow in a tube. Celebrity dermatologist Dr. Sheila Farhang, M.D., also ventured into cosmetics with a line designed to deliver color and coverage to post-treatment skin. And for smoky-eye season, Anastasia Beverly Hills dropped a neutral eyeshadow palette that serves as an all-in-one toolkit.

As you transition your perfume wardrobe for fall, you'll appreciate this month's new releases — like Merit’s New Wave L’Extrait de Parfum, a spicy aroma that takes the floral fragrance category into a decidedly moodier realm. Korean brand Elorea, meanwhile, debuted a honeyed fragrance that's equal parts warm and sweet. And Joonbyrd entered the category with its own take on functional fragrance.
Keep scrolling to shop October 2026’s best beauty launches, as curated by Bustle’s beauty team.

“I recently learned that wearing perfume to the office is a faux pas, and ever since, I’ve been on the hunt for one I can get away with. Elorea’s Quiet Trace is my pick. As the name implies, it stays close to the skin rather than announcing itself to the entire room. The combination of honey and floral notes reminds me of Phlur’s Honey Moon — but if you found that one a little too sweet, this might be more your speed. At first spritz, you get the soapiness of gardenia before it settles into something warmer and muskier. I’m happily wearing it on weekends, too.” – Emma Stout, beauty writer

“I’m convinced that I look better with a tan, but until I can go on a beach vacation, this Haus Labs liquid bronzer will do the trick. It’s sheer enough that I don’t have to worry about going overboard, but still delivers enough pigment to add some much-needed color back to my complexion. Even better, it leaves behind a hydrated finish — courtesy of its 70% skin care ingredients — that makes everything look much more believable. Call me a catfish, but I’ll be faking my summer glow until further notice.” – ES

“Dewsy has always been about high-quality body care, and its latest retinol-infused cream is giving my skin a serious upgrade. The formula is powered by 0.1% retinol, copper peptides, and ceramides — a combination that hydrates, smooths, and brightens. I’ve been using it after showering for the past few weeks, and my skin looks noticeably brighter, feels more hydrated, and is smoother to the touch. Even my husband has commented on the difference. And that’s when you know it’s good — that man notices nothing.” — Shyema Azam, beauty director, branded content

“With all the red light therapy masks hitting the market, it takes a lot to make one stand out — but JOVS’ latest makes a compelling case for the splurge. Unlike traditional LED masks, it combines laser light therapy with a 10-electrode EMS system designed to stimulate facial muscles, essentially bringing two treatments together in one. Its multi-wavelength light technology and customizable settings let you tailor each session, whether you’re looking to boost radiance, support collagen, or target the appearance of sagging and loss of definition. I love how comfortably snug the mask feels, and the attached remote makes it easy to switch between treatment modes and seven EMS intensity levels. After my first week of use, my skin looked and felt more refreshed, and after a month, I noticed it looked slightly firmer, too. It's definitely a luxury purchase, but for anyone looking to level up their at-home skin care routine, this offers more than your average light therapy mask.” — SA

“I will tell people until I’m blue in the face that they need to try Makeup By Mario’s lip pencils, so naturally, I couldn’t get my hands on the new Lip Trip Gift Set fast enough. Featuring minis of three bestselling shades — Toasty, Smokey Pink, and Travis — the full-coverage matte pencils create the perfect lip base, while the brand’s lip-lock technology helps keep your look in place through every holiday party, cocktail hour, and festive gathering to come.” — SA

“I may have found my dream fall eyeshadow palette, and I haven’t been able to put it down since it landed on my vanity. With 12 shades spanning taupe, brown, and mauve, plus a mix of velvety mattes and light-catching shimmers, there's something for every mood. The formulas blend effortlessly, making it easy to create everything from a soft, lived-in wash of color to the smokiest, most sultry eye look.” — SA

“If you love a dark, moody fragrance for fall, Arabian Mate is worth a sniff. It opens with bright bergamot and lemon before giving way to spiced pear and cardamom, followed by a floral heart of rose, jasmine, and saffron. The dry-down, though, is where it gets particularly interesting: Oud, sandalwood, vanilla, and amber give it a cozy, subtly sweet finish that smells utterly rich.” — Rachel Lapidos, deputy beauty editor

“The industry-beloved LED mask just got an upgrade with the launch of Series 3. It retains the same comfortable silicone design and six clinically backed wavelengths, but now comes with a companion MyDose app that lets you track and customize your treatments. It's a smarter, more personalized way to get your red light therapy at home.” — RL

“With the Joonbyrd Mood Jelly sticks, fragrance application is a little more fun. The solid perfume delivers a mood boost through its feel-good scent and satisfyingly squishy jelly texture — perfect for tossing in your bag for an easy swipe-and-sniff self-care moment.” — RL

“La Roche-Posay is among the first brands to bring BEMT, the first new sunscreen filter approved by the FDA in more than 25 years, to the U.S. market. The innovative filter is now part of the brand’s cult-favorite Anthelios formula, giving you the same hydrating sun protection you know and love with an upgrade in UV-filter technology.” — RL

“My first impression of Merit’s second fragrance? Incredibly sexy. Its sensual blend of incense, woods, and green aromatics is softened by a touch of vanilla, creating a scent that feels unexpected and a little addictive. It's the kind of fragrance that leaves you wanting another sniff.” — RL

“I don’t love overly sweet gourmands in perfume form, but when it comes to body care, I’m all about decadence. Enter: e.l.f.’s Spicy Bundt body cream. The deeply hydrating formula melts into skin without feeling heavy, and makes you smell like an irresistible dessert.” — RL

“In case you haven’t heard, Tate McRae has officially joined the celebrity fragrance club. Tate 01 is the pop star’s take on a white floral, but as it wears, notes of amber, sandalwood, and tonka emerge, giving the scent a warmer, more intimate, skin-like quality.” — RL
14The Multifunctional Foundation

“After years of patients asking what makeup they could safely wear after in-office procedures, dermatologist Dr. Sheila Farhang decided to create something herself. Enter Dose of Derm, her take on the skin care-meets-makeup category. The All-in-One Clinical Foundation combines mineral-based sun protection and breathable coverage with longevity-focused ingredients, including exosomes, peptides, and vitamin C — exactly the kind of multitasking formula you'd hope for from a dermatologist-founded makeup line.” — RL

“Leave it to Glow Recipe to create the ultimate blurred lip essential. The soft-matte formula contains vegan PDRN, panthenol, and hyaluronic acid for pillowy-soft hydration — meaning no emphasized lip lines. The tapered tip makes application a breeze, whether you're lining or filling in your pout. It feels like cushiony air on your lips — truly mind-blowingly lightweight. I'm obsessed with every single shade, but Set The Tone, a rosy beige, is my current fave for everyday wear.” — RL
16The Luminizing Body Lotion

“Old Navy Beauty Co. has added another fragrance to its lineup: Shimmer Sparkle, a luxe gourmand with notes of salted caramel, crystallized sugar, and quince. This body lotion lets you wear the scent while delivering lasting hydration and a subtle shimmer — an ideal find for your holiday party circuit.” — RL

“This is the first chocolate-forward fragrance I've fallen in love with. You know that first sip of your latte when it's been made just right? That's the vibe of Mocha Magic. Rich espresso, mocha, biscotti, toffee, vanilla, and bourbon mingle in this creamy gourmand that I simply can't stop talking about.” — RL

“Praise be: Facialist Sofie Pavitt has brought her signature hot-cold therapy treatment from her facial studio to your vanity with the Temp Check mask duo. Start with the warming mask for gentle, enzyme-based exfoliation, then cool things down with the hydrating exosome mask (yes, it actually feels cold). The result? A pro-level glow in just 20 minutes.” — RL

“This limited-edition lip oil from Gisou is the candy-coated gloss of millennial dreams. It appears dark in the tube, but the shade blends into a milky, sheer red for a perfect, on-the-go autumn look — not to mention, the flavor is fabulous.” — Samantha Nik, director of talent relations, BDG
“Meet your new joy stick. With its balmy universal highlighter and rich, smoky eyeliner, this duo is made for your upcoming slate of holiday parties — or just a Tuesday afternoon.” — SN
21The Travel-Friendly Must-Have

“The coquette collab we didn’t know we needed (but most definitely did). Beauty tool guru Lauryn Bosstick and Djerf Avenue founder Matilda Djerf teamed up to give some of their beauty favorites a makeover in the Swedish fashion brand’s Summer Berries print. Each collection also comes with a limited-edition pair of PJs and a matching robe.” — SN

“I’m going to say it how it is: This is a salmon sperm facial in a bottle. After trying the Marini Reboot serum during a treatment, I was immediately sold. Its salmon-derived PDRN helps support collagen production and calm inflammation, while squalane delivers a dose of deep hydration and helps reinforce the skin barrier. Consider it a little post-facial magic for your everyday routine.” — SN

“A supermodel founder’s best-kept beauty secret? This sheet mask. Unwrap the pink packaging to reveal a completely clear jelly mask, then wear it for 15 minutes for skin that looks like you’ve gotten a full eight hours of sleep. Powered by vegan PDRN — aka the California roll version of the salmon sperm facial — plus glycerin, hyaluronic acid, and niacinamide, this pretty little mask leaves skin looking plumper, smoother, and dewier before happy hour.” — SN

items.title: Exclusive: The 'Hunger Games' Team Didn't Listen To Fan Casting For This Reason
items.description: The Hunger Games Team Didn’t Listen To Fan Casting For This Reason
items.author: Jake Viswanath
paragraphs: The Hunger Games Team Didn’t Listen To Fan Casting For This Reason
Sunrise on the Reaping director Francis Lawrence and producer Nina Jacobson reveal how they cast the new prequel.

When the cast of the new Hunger Games prequel Sunrise on the Reaping was announced one-by-one on social media, fans saw their dream casting come to life, from Mckenna Grace as District 12’s sassiest tribute, Maysilee Donner, to Elle Fanning stepping into Elizabeth Banks’ pastel wigs as Effie Trinket. Each reveal felt like Christmas came early, but despite how it looked, fans didn’t cast the movie.

In an exclusive interview with Bustle, Sunrise on the Reaping director Francis Lawrence and producer Nina Jacobson opened up about fan casting, admitting they love Suzanne Collins’ iconic book series as much as the fandom — but they didn’t intentionally listen to them.

“We don't go to fan casting feeds and make our lists based on that,” Lawrence said. “When Elle talks about the fans wanting her, she's 100% right, but she was at the top of our list of people to go to. She and I had worked together before, and she was who I wanted to play Effie. It just also is the fan choice.”

As Jacobson explained, she and Lawrence found out that Collins was writing Sunrise on the Reaping “way earlier” than any of her prior books, giving them extra time to adapt the novel into the film. “There was a long, long period where we could imagine our cast before people even knew the book was happening,” she says.

“We knew we wanted Jesse [Plemons] before the book was announced. We knew we wanted Elle before the book was announced,” Lawrence adds. “There are many, many, many people that we knew that we wanted to go for before anybody even knew there was a book.”

However, when the two realized their own hopes aligned with the fans, they knew they were on the right track. “It’s very easy for us to pay attention because we are the fans,” Jacobson says. “There’s very little distance ever between who they’re hoping for and who we envision because we’re kind of a hive mind in that regard.”

She went on to praise fans for trusting the creative team’s instincts and giving them the freedom other franchises usually don’t get. “I do think that we have the smartest, most thoughtful and expansive fans,” she says. “They’re not that kind of rigid haters whose things have to be exactly a certain way, or it’s not the way it’s supposed to be. There are a lot of franchises where the fans are like an albatross in a way. You need them, but you’re always worrying about them.”

items.title: Your November Horoscope Is Here — & Now Get Radically Honest About What You Want
items.description: Cosmic beings, November begins at a slower pace than we may be craving, but the second half of the month has some serious comeback energy written all over it. Scorpio Season continues through the first three weeks of November, encouraging us to dig deeper into
items.author: Dossé-Via Trenou
paragraphs: Cosmic beings, November begins at a slower pace than we may be craving, but the second half of the month has some serious comeback energy written all over it. Scorpio Season continues through the first three weeks of November, encouraging us to dig deeper into our desires, confront our shadows, and get radically honest about what we want from life. With Mercury retrograde in Scorpio and Venus retrograde in Libra as the month begins, communication, relationships, money, and creativity are all still under review.

The energy starts shifting on November 9th, when the Scorpio New Moon strikes and invites us to set intentions around personal power, transformation, and emotional honesty. This lunation is especially potent because Scorpio’s traditional ruler, Mars, is in bold, passionate Leo, while its modern ruler, Pluto, is moving forward in innovative Aquarius. Both placements encourage us to take ownership of our futures, even if doing so requires us to confront some uncomfortable truths. Mercury and Venus  retrograde have spent weeks showing us what we needed to see, whether we liked it or not. Now the Scorpio New Moon asks a much more direct question: what are you going to do about it? The 10 days following this lunation are especially powerful for setting intentions that reflect who you are becoming, rather than who you’ve been conditioned to be.

Then on November 13th, both Mercury and Venus end their retrogrades, and the second half of the month can feel like a much-needed breath of fresh air. We’ll still be navigating the post-retrograde shadows for a few weeks, but forward momentum becomes easier to access. On November 22nd, Sagittarius Season begins, bringing fire, laughter, curiosity, and a renewed appetite for adventure after Scorpio Season took us through the emotional depths. The Gemini Full Moon on November 24th adds to that liberating energy, encouraging us to release the mental and emotional heaviness we’ve been carrying and remember that there’s a whole world beyond the situations we’ve been obsessing over.

And just when we’re ready to fly off into the sunset, Mars enters Virgo on November 25th and reminds us that the details still matter, babes. The end of November encourages us to get practical about the lives we’re creating: paying bills, organizing our environments, tending to our health, scheduling appointments, and simplifying routines that have become unnecessarily complicated. November ends with a beautiful reminder that the life we envision becomes more achievable when our everyday choices begin reflecting it.
Read your horoscopes for your Sun and Rising signs for the most in-depth forecast.

Aries, November begins with Scorpio Season pulling you into some of the deepest corners of your emotional world. Your intimacy, shared resources, and transformation zone is activated, and the Scorpio New Moon on November 9th could mark a powerful turning point in how you approach trust, vulnerability, and the things you share with others. With your ruling planet Mars in Leo, there’s a part of you that’s ready to reclaim your power and move forward. Just remember that transformation takes more than one  dramatic declaration. Give yourself room to shed the layers.

November 13th brings a double dose of relief as Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio and Venus ends hers in Libra. Mercury direct can help untangle misunderstandings involving intimacy, finances, or complicated emotional dynamics, while Venus direct in your partnership sector gives your closest relationships a chance to find their footing again. If the past few weeks have felt like an ongoing episode of What Are We Actually  Doing Here?, you may finally start getting some answers. Some Aries will feel ready to recommit, while others may realize they’ve been doing too much emotional heavy lifting. Either way, you’ll have a clearer sense of what reciprocity should look like.

Then Sag Season begins on November 22nd, activating your adventure, travel, and expansion sector and bringing back that spontaneous spark you’ve been missing. The Gemini Full Moon on November 24th lights up your communication realm, potentially bringing an important conversation, announcement, or writing project to a culmination. And when Mars enters Virgo on November 25th, your attention shifts toward your health, work, and daily routines. You may suddenly feel motivated to organize your schedule, clean up your habits, and get your life together before the year ends. Start with the little things, Aries. They’ll add up faster than you think.

Taurus, November begins with Scorpio Season shining a spotlight on your closest relationships, and you may be learning more about yourself through the people you love than you expected. With the sun moving through your partnership sector for the first three weeks of the month, questions around commitment, trust, intimacy, and reciprocity become harder to ignore. The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th could open a meaningful new chapter in a romantic or professional partnership, especially if you’ve been craving more emotional honesty. Just make sure you’re being honest with yourself about what you need, rather than agreeing to something simply because it feels familiar.

November 13th is a particularly significant date for you because your ruling planet, Venus, ends its retrograde in Libra, while Mercury simultaneously ends its retrograde in Scorpio. If your relationships have felt like one long game of emotional detective work lately, you may finally get to put the magnifying glass down. Mercury direct in your partnership sector makes it easier to communicate your feelings and understand where someone else is coming from, while Venus direct in your wellness and daily-routine sector helps you recognize which habits have been supporting your peace and which ones have been disrupting it. You may realize that certain relationship dynamics have been affecting your physical and emotional well-being more than you initially thought. Let that awareness guide your next steps.

Then Sag Season begins on November 22nd, shifting your focus toward intimacy, shared finances, and the deeper commitments you’re ready to make. The Gemini Full Moon on November 24th illuminates your money and self-worth sector, potentially bringing a financial milestone, an important purchase, or a realization about how much your time and energy are actually worth. And when Mars enters Virgo on November 25th, your creativity, romance, and pleasure sector gets a welcome boost. After  spending so much of November analyzing your relationships, you may be ready to flirt, create, laugh, and enjoy yourself again. Life is allowed to be delicious, Taurus.

Gemini, November begins with Scorpio Season asking you to take a closer look at how you’ve been treating yourself behind the scenes. Your health, work, and daily routines are under the cosmic microscope, and the Scorpio New Moon on November 9th could inspire you to make some long-overdue lifestyle changes. Scorpio energy wants you to get to the root of these patterns. With Mars in Leo energizing your communication zone, you may feel more motivated to speak up about what you need, set clearer boundaries, and stop treating exhaustion like a personality trait.

On November 13th, your ruling planet Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio, while Venus ends hers in Libra, and you may feel like someone finally turned the lights back on. If work has been chaotic, appointments have been rescheduled, or your usual routines have felt impossible to maintain, Mercury direct can help you regain a sense of order. Meanwhile, Venus direct brings fresh energy to your romance, creativity, and pleasure realm. As Venus moves forward, you’ll have a better understanding of what makes your heart feel genuinely excited and which connections deserve more of your attention.

Then Sag Season begins on November 22nd, illuminating your partnership zone and making relationships a major focus as the year winds down. But the real main-character moment arrives on November 24th with your annual Gemini Full Moon! This could be one of the most emotionally revealing lunations of your year, bringing a personal milestone, breakthrough, or realization about how much you’ve changed over the past six months. When Mars enters Virgo on November 25th, your attention shifts toward home, family, and creating a more supportive living environment.

Cancer, November begins with Scorpio Season bringing some much-needed passion,  playfulness, and creative inspiration into your world. As a fellow Water sign, Scorpio knows how to speak your emotional language, and with the sun illuminating your romance, pleasure, and inner-child realm for the first three weeks of November, you may feel more magnetic, expressive, and willing to follow your heart. The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th could mark a beautiful fresh start in your love life or inspire you to take a creative passion more seriously. With Mars in Leo activating your money and self-worth zone, you may also be realizing that your talents deserve to be valued, including financially. There’s something empowering about recognizing how much you have to offer without waiting for someone else to validate it first.

Then November 13th brings a welcome shift as Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio and Venus ends hers in Libra. If your romantic life has been giving mixed signals, or you’ve been second-guessing a creative decision, Mercury direct can help you understand what you actually want. Venus direct in your home and family realm may also bring relief after weeks of revisiting domestic tensions, family dynamics, or questions about where you truly belong. The second half of November gives you more room to make decisions from a place of emotional clarity rather than reacting to every little thing that comes up.

Sag Season begins on November 22nd, shifting your attention toward work, wellness, and getting your daily life into a rhythm that actually feels good. But before you start filling your calendar with a million responsibilities, the Gemini Full Moon on November 24th illuminates your spirituality and solitude zone, encouraging you to release emotional baggage you’ve been carrying for far too long. When Mars enters Virgo on November 25th, your communication and learning realm becomes energized, making the final weeks of the year ideal for writing, studying, having important conversations, and getting organized mentally. Your intuition has been speaking loudly all month, Cancer. Now it’s time to put some of those insights into words.

Leo, November begins with Scorpio Season drawing your attention toward home, family, and the emotional roots that have shaped who you are today. You may feel more nostalgic than usual, or find yourself questioning whether your current living environment truly reflects the person you’re becoming. The Scorpio New Moon on  November 9th could inspire a fresh start involving your home life, a family relationship, or even your definition of belonging. With Mars still moving through your sign, you’ve got plenty of fire and ambition to make things happen, but Scorpio Season may reveal that some of your biggest breakthroughs are happening behind closed doors.

November 13th brings some welcome clarity as Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio and Venus ends hers in Libra. If family conversations have been going in circles, household plans have been delayed, or you’ve been questioning a decision about where to live, Mercury direct can help you sort through the confusion. Meanwhile, Venus direct in your communication and immediate-environment zone may make it easier to reconnect with siblings, neighbors, or people you’ve had misunderstandings with lately. Give people a chance to show you they’ve grown, Leo, while remembering that you get to decide how much access they have to your life.

Then Sag Season begins on November 22nd, and as a fellow Fire sign, you may feel like someone finally turned the music back up! Your romance, creativity, and pleasure realm comes alive, encouraging you to flirt, celebrate, and make more room for whatever brings you joy. The Gemini Full Moon on November 24th illuminates your friendship and community zone, potentially bringing an exciting collaboration, or a realization about which friendships have evolved over the past six months. Some connections may naturally fade while others become stronger. And when Mars leaves your sign and enters Virgo on November 25th, your focus shifts toward money, self worth, and financial organization. You’ll have spent weeks rediscovering what matters emotionally, and now you’ll be ready to invest your time, energy, and resources  accordingly.

Virgo, November begins with Scorpio Season encouraging you to pay closer attention to the conversations you’re having, both with others and with yourself. Your communication, learning, and immediate environment are activated for the first three weeks of the month, and you may find yourself craving more meaningful exchanges rather than endless small talk. The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th could inspire you to begin a writing project, deepen your studies, or finally express something you’ve been keeping to yourself.

November 13th is especially significant because your ruling planet Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio, while Venus ends hers in Libra. If you’ve been dealing with misunderstandings, delayed responses, technology mishaps, or conversations that seem to go absolutely nowhere, Mercury direct can help you find your words again. Venus direct in your money and self-worth zone may also bring greater clarity around your finances, spending habits, and the value you place on your own skills. The second half of November gives you an opportunity to make more confident decisions about what deserves your time and resources.

Then Sag Season begins on November 22nd, shifting your attention toward home. You may feel inspired to make your living space more comfortable or reconnect with loved ones as the holidays approach. The Gemini Full Moon on November 24th illuminates your career and public-image realm, potentially bringing recognition, a professional milestone, or an important realization about where your ambitions are taking you. Something you’ve been building over the past six months could finally bear fruit. And on  November 25th, Mars enters your sign, Virgo, giving you a serious boost of motivation and personal drive. With Mars preparing for an extended stay in your sign, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to reinvent your routines, strengthen your confidence, and take the lead in shaping your next chapter.

Libra, November begins with Scorpio Season encouraging you to get serious about your money, self-worth, and the kind of security you want to create for yourself. After a birthday season that may have brought plenty of personal revelations, the sun’s journey through Scorpio asks you to examine how your financial choices reflect your evolving priorities. The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th could inspire you to rethink your income streams, negotiate better compensation, or finally confront a spending habit that’s been draining your resources. With Mars in Leo energizing your friendship and community realm, the people around you may play an important role in helping you recognize opportunities you hadn’t considered. Just be mindful of comparing your progress to someone else’s highlight reel.

November 13th is a major turning point for you, Libra, because your ruling planet Venus finally ends its retrograde in your sign, on the same day Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio. Whew! If the past several weeks have felt like an unsolicited personality audit, you may be more than ready to graduate from all that introspection. Venus direct can help you feel more comfortable in your skin again, especially if you’ve been questioning your appearance, relationships, or the direction your life is taking. Meanwhile, Mercury direct brings greater clarity to financial decisions that may have been delayed or complicated.

Then Sag Season begins on November 22nd, lighting up your communication, learning, and immediate-environment zone. Your social butterfly tendencies may return in full force, and you could feel inspired to reconnect with friends, explore your neighborhood, or share ideas you’ve been keeping to yourself. The Gemini Full Moon on November 24th activates your expansion realm, potentially bringing a breakthrough involving a trip, academic pursuit, publishing project, or long-term dream you’ve been nurturing for months. And when Mars enters Virgo on November 25th, your solitude and spirituality zone becomes activated, encouraging you to balance all that outward excitement with some much-needed rest.

Scorpio, happy birthday season! If there’s one sign that deserves to feel like they’re emerging from a chrysalis this November, it’s you. You’ve spent the past several weeks confronting old versions of yourself, questioning your desires, and shedding emotional layers you may have carried for years. And with the sun in your sign for the first three weeks of November, you’re finally getting a chance to celebrate the person you’re becoming.

The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th is especially powerful because it marks your annual cosmic rebirth, with Mars in Leo and Pluto in Aquarius encouraging you to reclaim your confidence and take your destiny into your own hands. Think back to who you were six months ago, or even at the beginning of the year. You’ve survived transformations that once felt impossible to navigate, and now you’re standing at the threshold of a new chapter. Let yourself get excited about it, Scorpio. You’ve earned this  moment.

November 13th brings another reason to celebrate as Mercury finally ends its retrograde in your sign, while Venus ends hers in Libra. Whew, enough character development already! Mercury direct helps you feel more confident expressing your thoughts, making decisions, and moving toward goals that may have been on pause. Meanwhile, Venus direct in your spirituality and solitude zone can bring emotional closure to situations you’ve been privately processing. You may notice that certain memories or relationships no longer have the same hold over you. That freedom is worth celebrating just as much as any external milestone.

Then Sag Season begins on November 22nd, shifting your focus toward money, self-worth, and building tangible security around this new version of yourself. The Gemini Full Moon on November 24th illuminates your intimacy realm, potentially bringing a breakthrough involving trust, financial commitments, or an emotional bond that’s been evolving over the past six months. You may finally feel ready to release something you’ve been holding onto out of loyalty or fear of the unknown. And when Mars enters Virgo on November 25th, your friendship, community, and future-goals zone gets energized, helping you connect with people who genuinely support your evolution. Your next chapter is calling, Scorpio, and you get to decide who has a front-row seat.

Sag, can you feel it? Your birthday season is right around the corner, but first, Scorpio  Season has a few final layers it wants you to shed. For the first three weeks of  November, the sun moves through your spirituality, solitude, and subconscious realm,  encouraging you to embrace a little hibernation before your annual comeback. The  Scorpio New Moon on November 9th is a powerful opportunity for shadow work,  emotional purging, and releasing the fears that have been keeping you attached to an outdated version of yourself. With Mars in Leo activating your adventure zone, part of you is already dreaming about your next big move. There’s something beautiful about clearing out your emotional closet before stepping into a brand-new solar chapter.

November 13th brings a welcome sense of relief as Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio and Venus ends hers in Libra. Mercury direct can help you make sense of the vivid dreams, resurfacing memories, and private revelations that have been occupying your mind lately. You may finally understand why a certain chapter needed to end or why you’ve been feeling unusually withdrawn. Meanwhile, Venus direct in your friendship and community realm helps you gain clarity about your social circle,  especially if old friends have resurfaced or certain group dynamics have felt off. As the retrograde fog begins to lift, your natural optimism may start returning, and you’ll feel increasingly ready to rejoin the world.

And then, on November 22nd, Sagittarius Season officially begins! Happy birthday, Sag! After weeks of emotional excavation, the sun enters your sign and brings a surge of confidence, charisma, curiosity, and main-character energy. You may feel like booking a trip, reinventing your look, saying yes to new experiences, or simply reminding everyone why you’re the life of the party. The Gemini Full Moon on November 24th illuminates your partnership realm, bringing an important relationship milestone or revelation about who deserves to accompany you into this next chapter. Some connections may deepen beautifully, while others reveal that you’ve outgrown their dynamics. When Mars enters Virgo on November 25th, your career and public-image zone becomes energized, giving you the drive to turn your birthday-season inspiration into professional progress. The year may be winding down, but for you, a whole new adventure is just beginning.

Capricorn, November begins with Scorpio Season encouraging you to take a closer look at the people you’re surrounding yourself with and the future you’re working so hard to create. Your friendships, community, and long-term aspirations are highlighted for the first three weeks of the month, and you may feel more selective about who gets access to your time and energy. The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th could mark a fresh start involving a friendship, collaboration, or dream you’ve been nurturing behind the scenes. You don’t have to build an empire entirely on your own, Capricorn, even if you’ve gotten pretty good at it.

November 13th brings a shift in momentum as Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio and Venus ends hers in Libra. If you’ve been reconsidering a friendship, dealing with misunderstandings within a group, or questioning whether a long-term goal still excites you, Mercury direct can help you see the situation more clearly. Meanwhile, Venus direct in your career and reputation zone may bring relief after weeks of professional uncertainty or reevaluating your relationship with success. As both planets move forward, you may feel more confident about the people you want to work with and the professional legacy you’re building.

Then Sag Season begins on November 22nd, inviting you into your annual period of rest, reflection, and spiritual renewal before your own birthday season arrives in December. The Gemini Full Moon on November 24th illuminates your work, health, and daily-routine realm, potentially bringing a project to completion or revealing which habits have been quietly draining your energy. You may realize that your schedule needs some  serious editing before the year ends. And when Mars enters fellow earth sign Virgo on November 25th, your expansion zone gets a powerful boost. There’s a whole world beyond your responsibilities, Capricorn, and the end of November is encouraging you to remember that.

Aquarius, November begins with Scorpio Season putting your ambitions, career, and public image under the cosmic spotlight. You may be feeling more determined than ever to make a name for yourself, but also more aware of the pressure that comes with being  seen and recognized. The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th could mark a powerful professional turning point, whether you’re preparing to launch something, step into a leadership role, or completely redefine what success looks like for you. With Pluto in your sign and Mars in Leo activating your partnership realm, the people you align yourself with could have a significant influence on your next chapter.

November 13th brings some much-needed clarity as Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio and Venus ends hers in Libra. If professional conversations have been delayed, you’ve been second-guessing a career decision, or you’ve felt misunderstood by people in positions of authority, Mercury direct can help you regain your confidence and communicate your intentions more effectively. Meanwhile, Venus direct in your travel realm may revive your excitement about opportunities that felt uncertain over the past several weeks. As both planets move forward, you may realize that your ambitions have evolved considerably, and you’re ready to pursue opportunities that reflect your current values.

Then Sag Season begins on November 22nd, bringing a welcome shift toward friendship, community, and the dreams you want to bring to life with others. After weeks of taking your professional responsibilities so seriously, you may finally feel like getting out, meeting new people, and remembering that life is supposed to be fun, too. The Gemini Full Moon on November 24th illuminates your romance, creativity, and pleasure zone, potentially bringing a love story, creative project, or personal passion to an  exciting culmination. And when Mars enters Virgo on November 25th, your intimacy, shared-finances, and transformation realm becomes energized, encouraging you to get serious about emotional boundaries, and the resources you share with others. You’re ending November with a clearer sense of what deserves your commitment.

Pisces, November begins with Scorpio Season awakening your desire to explore, evolve, and experience more of what life has to offer. As a fellow Water sign, Scorpio energy tends to resonate deeply with you, and for the first three weeks of the month, your expansion realm is activated. You may feel increasingly drawn toward a new destination, a different philosophy, or a dream that once seemed too far-fetched to pursue. The Scorpio New Moon on November 9th could mark the beginning of an exciting new chapter involving travel, education, or spiritual growth. With Mars in Leo  energizing your routine zone, you may also realize that making these bigger dreams happen requires some adjustments to your everyday schedule.

November 13th brings a welcome shift as Mercury ends its retrograde in Scorpio and Venus ends hers in Libra. If travel plans have been delayed, you’ve been questioning your educational or professional direction, or a certain belief system no longer feels aligned with who you are, Mercury direct can help you find clarity. Meanwhile, Venus direct in your intimacy realm may bring resolution to financial or emotional matters that have felt complicated lately. The second half of November encourages you to recognize where healthier boundaries could create more room for genuine closeness.

Then Sag Season begins on November 22nd, putting your career, reputation, and long-term ambitions in the spotlight. You may feel more visible professionally or inspired to pursue an opportunity that stretches you beyond your comfort zone. The Gemini Full Moon on November 24th illuminates your home and family realm, potentially bringing a turning point involving your living situation, a family relationship, or your sense of  belonging. And when Mars enters Virgo on November 25th, your partnership zone gets a major boost of energy. With Mars beginning an extended stay in this part of your  chart, the coming months will teach you plenty about collaboration, compromise, and choosing people who are genuinely willing to grow alongside you.

items.title: 13 Actually-Good Beauty Stocking Stuffers Under $25
items.description: 13 Actually-Good Beauty Stocking Stuffers Under $25
items.author: Karina Hoshikawa
paragraphs: 13 Actually-Good Beauty Stocking Stuffers Under $25

At Refinery29, we’re here to help you navigate this overwhelming world of stuff. All of our market picks are independently selected and curated by the editorial team. All product details reflect the price and availability at the time of publication. If you buy or click on something we link to on our site, Refinery29 may earn commission.
Morphe Totally Set Mini Brighten & Set Powder Duo

Consider this your two-step shortcut to a soft-focus, airbrushed finish. This travel-friendly duo includes Morphe’s Bake & Set powders in a brightening pink shade to perk up the under-eyes and a sheer translucent formula to lock makeup in place without adding extra coverage. It’s a handy little set for touch-ups on the go, too.
The Ordinary The Mini Essentials Set

Serums are the workhorse of any good skincare routine, and this set lets you put three of The Ordinary’s bestsellers to the test. It includes travel-friendly sizes of Niacinamide 10% + Zinc 1% to help minimize the look of pores and balance excess oil, Hyaluronic Acid 2% + B5 for a boost of plumping hydration, and Soothing & Barrier Support Serum to help strengthen the skin barrier.

This limited-edition Starface set includes three mini packs of the brand’s iconic Hydro-Star pimple patches, all tucked into a keepsake pink zip pouch inspired by its instantly recognizable compact. Cute, practical, and guaranteed to come in handy when a breakout shows up uninvited.
Benefit Cosmetics Mini Beneville Fruit Stand Lash & Brow Gift Set

If there are two things Benefit knows how to do, it’s brows and lashes. This mini gift set brings together two of the brand’s bestsellers: BADgal BANG! Volumizing Mascara for full, fanned-out lashes and the beloved 24-HR Brow Setter Clear Gel for fluffy, defined arches.
Fenty Beauty Gloss Bomb Prismatic Lip Luminizer

Who wouldn't love to find a little Fenty hanging on the tree? This ornament-sized Gloss Bomb features a multidimensional burgundy hue that adds a festive wash of shimmer to any holiday lip combo. It's also the perfect stocking stuffer for the Fenty fan in your life (or a cute little treat for yourself).
Rare Beauty Luminous Faves Lip Duo

Consider this your shortcut to a festive, party-ready pout. Rare Beauty’s lip duo includes full sizes of the Kind Words Matte Lip Liner in Lovely and Positive Light Luminizing Lip Gloss in an exclusive champagne shimmer shade that you can only get in this set. Wear them together for a softly defined, glossy lip or mix and match with your other favorites.
Peach & Lily Double Cleanse Mini Duo

The secret to a fresh, glowy complexion starts with a good cleanse — and Peach & Lily makes it easy with this double-cleansing duo. The set pairs an oil cleanser that melts away makeup and SPF with a hydrating gel face wash to leave skin feeling clean, refreshed, and ready for the rest of your routine.

Glossier always brings something fun to the holiday lineup, and this year, it’s giving us a fresh reason to stock up on its cult-favorite Balm Dotcom. Meet Just Baked, a limited-edition flavor that captures the sweetness of fresh-from-the-oven sugar cookies, complete with a pretty mauve tint for a festive finishing touch.

Get your glow on this season with BYOMA’s hydration-focused set, featuring travel-friendly minis of the Creamy Jelly Cleanser, Hydrating Serum, and Moisturizing Gel-Cream. Each formula is powered by the brand’s signature ceramide complex to help support the skin barrier, making this trio a great pick for anyone looking to keep their complexion happy, hydrated, and dewy.
Bath & Body Works Snowflakes & Cashmere Fine Fragrance Mist

Bath & Body Works knows its way around a holiday fragrance, and Snowflakes & Cashmere is proof. Fronted by the impossibly charming Zooey Deschanel, this cozy scent blends warm vanilla cashmere cream with decadent caramel woods and a hint of frosted clementine for a sweet, sophisticated take on winter perfume.
Laneige Midnight Minis Lip Sleeping Mask 5 pc. Gift Set

Who needs kisses under the mistletoe when you have five flavors of Laneige’s cult-favorite Lip Sleeping Mask to keep your lips feeling soft and hydrated? This set includes everything from the OG Berry to limited-edition Mango and my personal favorite, Vanilla, making it a sweet little treat for any lip-care lover on your list.
Being Frenshe Wind Down Ritual Set

Give the gift of a little R&R without the heavy investment. Being Frenshe’s Wind Down Ritual Set features the brand’s calming Lavender Cloud scent in a Hair, Body & Linen Mist and Restoring Lip Balm, plus limited-edition soothing eye patches and plush socks for a full-on self-care moment.

This seriously stacked advent calendar, which includes a mix of 25 full- and travel-size products from luxury brands like Summer Fridays, Ouai, Dr. Dennis Gross, and more.
